energy_budget.note: Debye U=C T/4. From 1 K to 4 K takes only ~5.5 aJ. That is ~15 fully absorbed 532 nm photons, or ~40 absorbed 532 nm photons after a Stokes-and-QE correction of 0.39. Continuous allowed power over 3 s, with no cooling, is ~2 aW.

gas.formula: P = 2 π R^2 α (p/T_g) <v> (T_p-T_g), <v>=sqrt(8kT/πm), monatomic 2k per collision (DERIVED).

NV_readout.note: 100 μW, 1 μm waist, one NV, heat fraction 0.39. The 1→4 K budget is spent in a few tens of microseconds of illumination in vacuum. A typical millisecond ODMR pulse is far over budget if it happens in XHV before the hold.

leak_300K.note: A full 300 K bath, even with type IIa mid-IR absorption, deposits far more than 5 aJ in 3 s. Tight 4 K (or 1 K) radiation shields are mandatory; a room-temperature window in line of sight is not a small correction.

eddy_and_MW.note: For insulating type IIa diamond, eddy current dissipation from this slow Stern–Gerlach ramp is negligible (DERIVED: even a 2 nm graphite shell at σ~10^5 S/m gives ~10^{-29} W). A graphitic shell plus 2.87 GHz MW drive is the only plausible eddy risk and is not quantified here without a field geometry. Dielectric MW heating at tanδ=10^{-5} with a modest E also sits below the aW budget for short π-pulses; tanδ=10^{-2} and a high-E near-field antenna would need a dedicated estimate (ASSUMED not binding if pulses are short and the diamond is clean).

literature.hoang_li_2016: Hoang, Ahn, Bang, Li, Nat. Commun. 7, 12250 (2016): optically levitated NV nanodiamond, ESR thermometry. T from ~300 K at 1 atm to >450 K at 31 Torr under the trapping laser. Heating plus 1550/1064 nm ionization of NV−.
literature.rahman_frangeskou_2016: Rahman, Frangeskou, et al., Sci. Rep. 6, 21633 (2016): optically levitated NV nanodiamonds burn in air; in N2 they graphitize below ≈10 mbar and vanish by ≈2 mbar. Internal T ≈ 750–800 K at 300–380 mW of 1064 nm while gas cooling still works. Not melting.
literature.frangeskou_2018: Frangeskou, Rahman, Williams, Barker, Morley, New J. Phys. 20, 043016 (2018), arXiv:1608.04724: milled high-purity CVD nanodiamonds showed no measurable 1064 nm heating up to ~300 mW at 3–4 mbar; commercial HPHT NV powder has been reported >800 K. Nitrogen and surface graphitic carbon, not the lattice, dominate NIR absorption.
literature.delord_hetet_2017: Delord, Nicolas, Bodini, Hétet, Appl. Phys. Lett. 111, 013101? / 111, (2017), arXiv:1701.06407: micron diamonds in a Paul trap (no IR trap laser). Green-laser heating alone: T up to 470 K at 700 μW, 1 mbar; 390 K at 40 μW, 0.2 mbar. Attributed to nitrogen in commercial HPHT powder. Particles lost from the trap below ~10^{-2} mbar under the green beam.
literature.pettit_2017: Pettit et al., J. Opt. Soc. Am. B 34, C31 (2017): coherent control of a single NV in an optically levitated nanodiamond. After an initial low-vacuum exposure (cleaning), T stayed near room temperature at 2.5 kPa across the powers they tested. Still an optical trap, still gas-cooled, not XHV.
literature.rahman_barker_2017: Rahman & Barker, Nat. Photonics 11, 634 (2017): anti-Stokes refrigeration of levitated Yb3+:YLF nanocrystals to 130 K. Demonstrated, but not diamond, and not below ~130 K.
literature.kern_2017: Kern, Jeske, Lau, Greentree, Jelezko, Twamley, Phys. Rev. B 95, 235306 (2017), arXiv:1701.08505: theory of optical cryocooling of NV- or SiV-doped microdiamonds. Predict |ΔT|>10 K below room temperature at <100 mW in vacuum for NV (high QE); SiV less promising because of lower quantum efficiency. Not demonstrated, and not a 4 K protocol.
literature.hsu_2016: Hsu, Ji, Lewandowski, D’Urso, Sci. Rep. 6, 30125 (2016): magneto-gravitational trap for diamagnetic diamond nanocrystal clusters, stable from atmosphere to high vacuum, no intrinsic trap heating. Feedback cooling of COM (not T_int) to <1 K in one degree of freedom. Loaded by spray at atmospheric pressure.
literature.elahi_2024: Elahi, Schut, Dana, Grinin, Bose, Mazumdar, Geraci, arXiv:2411.02325 (2024/25): diamagnetic microchip traps designed for the QGEM protocol (mm-scale Z-trap for a weak Stern–Gerlach axis, 100 Hz / 500–800 Hz). Static/quasi-static currents, intended to avoid optical heating. A design paper, not a demonstration of a cold 10^{-15} Pa particle.
literature.alpha_1064: Calorimetry on single-crystal CVD (Element Six): α ≈ 0.03 cm^{-1} at 1064 nm, rising toward the UV (0.7 cm^{-1} at 364 nm). Type IIa compilations often quote α < 0.05 cm^{-1} at 1064 nm. Mid-IR type IIa window: α ≈ 0.033–0.07 cm^{-1} at 10.6 μm (Thomas et al. / Crystran compilations).
literature.sigma_NV: NV− absorption cross section at 532 nm: 3.1(0.8)×10^{-17} cm^2 (two-photon-referenced one-photon value). ZPL values around 4×10^{-17} cm^2 also appear. We use 3.1×10^{-17} cm^2.

feasible_outline: Material: high-purity type IIa / optical-grade CVD, oxygen-terminated (no graphitic shell), as few NV centres as the witness allows (ideally one). This is the only way Im χ and 532/1064 absorption stay in the window-grade / single-NV regime.

Trap: all-magnetic (magneto-gravitational, Paul, or a QGEM microchip trap). No 1064 nm tweezer during pump-down or the 3 s run. Hsu 2016 demonstrated laser-free diamagnetic trapping of diamond from atmosphere to high vacuum; Elahi 2024 is the QGEM-shaped design. Not yet demonstrated at 10^{-15} Pa or at 4 K with a 5.6×10^{-15} kg particle.

Environment: a 4 K (ideally 1 K) cryostat with tight radiation shields. A 300 K view factor of 10^{-7}–10^{-4} (depending on mid-IR α) already exceeds the 3 s energy budget. No room-temperature windows in line of sight.

Load and thermalise with cold helium buffer gas at 4 K (or 1 K) while the magnetic trap is on. Gas cooling is fast (milliseconds to seconds) down to ~10^{-4}–10^{-6} Pa at 4 K, and is demonstrated physics, though not in this exact apparatus. Then pump toward 10^{-15} Pa with lasers off. The particle stays at T_int ≈ T_env because it is already there, not because it radiates.

Initialise the NV spin while gas cooling still works (or after contact/loading, before the final pump). A 100 μW, 1 μm-waist 532 nm beam on a single NV deposits the entire 1 K→4 K budget in tens of microseconds of net heat at vacuum. Do not initialise in XHV and then wait — radiation will not dump the heat in time.

During the 3 s interferometry: no 532, no 1064, only the slow Stern–Gerlach ramps and, if needed, short microwave π-pulses. Read the spin after recombination. Heating during a short final readout does not undo the already-written entanglement, but the pulse must still be short enough to preserve contrast.
demonstrated: Optical-trap heating and burning/graphitization of NV nanodiamonds in vacuum (Rahman 2016, Hoang/Li 2016).
Green-laser heating of micron HPHT diamonds in a Paul trap with no IR tweezer (Delord/Hétet 2017).
Reduced NIR heating in milled high-purity CVD nanodiamonds, still at a few mbar (Frangeskou 2018).
Diamagnetic / magneto-gravitational trapping of diamond from air to high vacuum, no intrinsic heating (Hsu 2016).
Anti-Stokes refrigeration of levitated Yb:YLF to 130 K (Rahman & Barker 2017) — not diamond, not 4 K.
Buffer-gas cooling of levitated particles in general, and 4 K cryostats in general.
not_demonstrated: A 5.6×10^{-15} kg, 0.73 μm diamond with one (or few) NV, oxygen-terminated, in a magnetic trap at 10^{-15} Pa and T_int ≤ 4 K.
Pump-down from buffer-gas pressures to 10^{-15} Pa around a trapped microdiamond in a 4 K apparatus.
Stern–Gerlach splitting and Humpty-Dumpty recombination of such a trapped particle at the Stage 12 field precision.
Optical cryocooling of diamond to (or anywhere near) 4 K. Kern et al. 2017 is theory for modest cooling below room temperature.
An emissivity coating that speeds radiative cooling enough to matter at 4 K without destroying the PPT witness (Stage 13: Im χ ≳ 10^{-3} already squeezes the 4 K point).
rejected: Optical trapping or even a 1 μW alignment beam at 1064 nm during the XHV run: lattice α V I is 10^6–10^{11} times the 3 s energy budget, even for optimistic α.
Relying on radiative cooling after a laser pulse: window-grade τ at 1–4 K is days; dirty-surface τ is minutes, still much longer than 3 s, and “dirty” already squeezes the witness at 4 K.
Raising THz emissivity with a coating to speed cooling: the same Im χ enters the Stage 13 decoherence budget and kills C near 4–6 K.
Laser refrigeration as the primary 4 K path: not demonstrated in diamond, requires a cooling laser (another absorption source), and existing theory aims at tens of kelvin below ambient, not 1–4 K.

verdict_one_liner: The 0.73 μm diamond has a 1 K heat capacity of 8.5×10^{-20} J/K; 5.5 aJ takes it from 1 K to 4 K. No optical beam can be on during the XHV run. The only feasible path is: start already cold in a 4 K (or 1 K) magnetically trapped, well-shielded cryostat, gas-cool, pump with lasers off, initialise before the final pump, read out after the hold. Radiative self-cooling and laser refrigeration will not get you there in time.
